newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Sept 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - Sept 6.

text.p: PRAVO - Finnish President Martti Ahtisaari will visit the Czech Republic from September 9-11. This will be the first visit of a Finnish head of state to the Czech Republic.
- RadioMobil, partly-owned by Deutsche Telekom, will begin offering its GSM phone service in the last week of September, becoming the sole competition to the Eurotel's current monopoly of the market.

- Minister of Trade and Industry, Vladimir Dlouhy, stated that in the last three years there has not been a single case of arms exports from the Czech Republic that went against the political or economic interests of the state.
- CEZ, which is investing in the Temelin nuclear power plant, has admitted that the construction of the plant could be delayed anywhere from 5-11 months.
- The financial situation in Aero Vodochody will be discussed during the government session on September 11. The government will discuss ways of decreasing the company's three billion crown debt.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Czech Republic and Japan are prepared to intensify business cooperation and foreign trade, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus stated at the start of his one week Asian visit yesterday where he met with representatives of the Japanese government.
- The current increase of supranational concerns in the Czech Republic could facilitate a decree from the Ministry of Finance for the easing of customs duty on high-tech products.
- Metrostav a.s. is planning to increase its basic capital by 150 million crowns by a stock issue and to increase it by a further 20 percent through its own finances.
- Software602 a.s., the largest local software manufacturer, previewed its new software package, 602proInternet, allowing access to the Internet.
